input: image is a rectangular R by C binary integer array with distinct mutable row objects; empty outer arrays and zero-width rows are allowed. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. Python integer inputs are plain int excluding bool; any separately declared floating probabilities are ordinary float.
return: The identical image object, with each original row horizontally reversed and each bit inverted.
mutation_aliasing: Intentionally writes input cells in place, preserving outer and row identities and lengths. Caller aliases observe updates. Distinct rows are required because repeated row identities would be transformed once per occurrence. No output matrix is allocated; the Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Every cell remains 0 or 1; indices and midpoint behavior are exact. Reading both endpoint values before either assignment handles an odd-length middle cell correctly. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(R * C + R + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Each row uses a two-ended scan and no copied row or hidden reversing buffer. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 424 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper definition, Solution wrapper, signatures, loops, built-in calls, comments/annotations, whitespace and terminal newline.
